title: North Dakota: A Guide to the Northern Prairie State

creators.name: Federal Writers' Project of the Works Progress Administration for the State of North Dakota

summary: "North Dakota: A Guide to the Northern Prairie State" is a historical guidebook written in the late 1930s as part of the American Guide Series. Compiled by members of the Federal Writers' Project of the Works Progress Administration, the text aims to provide a comprehensive survey of North Dakota, highlighting its geography, history, and cultural significance. The book serves both as a traveling companion for tourists and a resource for understanding the rich heritage of the state. The opening of the guide introduces readers to North Dakota's identity and the pride its citizens take in distinguishing it from its southern neighbor, South Dakota. It describes the state's contemporary character, shaped by historical narratives of exploration, agriculture, and economic evolution. The text outlines the major themes of the guide, including the state's natural setting, the impact of indigenous populations, and the development of agricultural practices over time. Through vivid imagery and historical context, the book provides a foundational understanding of North Dakota’s landscapes and the people who inhabit it. (This is an automatically generated summary.)
